0.long_answer: Follicular lymphoma can transform into a more aggressive form known as diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. This transformation process in some cases has been associated with an infection by the Epstein–Barr virus (EBV). EBV, which is also linked to other lymphoproliferative disorders, may contribute to the malignant progression by infecting B cells and altering their behavior, leading to a phenotype characteristic of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The role of EBV in this context is supported by studies that indicate EBV-associated transformation in a subset of follicular lymphomas.
